label: directed communication
definition: The first person or institution communicates with, requests or urges action from, or advises the second.
scope_notes: Ask/urge/persuade/tell/notify form the coherent dominant communication family used previously. Bare cooperation or replacement is excluded. Send-to without a recoverable communicative object can be ambiguous. Institutional recipients are permitted.

facts.reason: Clinton persuades Congress, directly expressing communication aimed at the second institution.
Torre asks Williams, giving the directed requester-to-addressee relation.
Lewinsky directly tells and asks Jordan. Telephoning his office is consistent but is not needed to infer the recipient.
Bush asks, talks with and urges Gorbachev. The praise row alone would not establish that the praise was addressed to him.
Both repeated rows explicitly say Clinton asks Congress; this latent tuple is retained separately from the other Clinton tuple.
